::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
China's structural answer to imec — a full-flow 200mm pilot fab (not a lab cleanroom) de-risking the R&D→pilot→industrialization gap for MEMS, silicon photonics and biosensor chips; founded 2013 with the CAS Shanghai microsystems lineage, it has served 1,000+ customers and incubated 20+ companies with aggregate valuation above ¥15 billion, and was named a national 'little giant' 专精特新 platform in 2025.
:::

**Chinese name:** 上海微技术工业研究院 (Shànghǎi Wēijìshù Gōngyè Yánjiūyuàn)

## What does this facility make?

Engineering/pilot wafers: MEMS sensors, silicon-photonic chips (built under Shanghai's municipal SiPh major special project), biosensor chips; PDK-based tape-out services rather than commercial volume.

## Why does it matter?

Pilot lines like SITRI's are the missing middle layer that export controls cannot block as easily as frontier tools — the country's specialty-silicon innovation capacity increasingly runs through such platforms; it anchors Jiading's 'More than Moore' sensor cluster.

## Project Timeline

- **Nov 2013** — Founded by Shanghai Municipal Commission of STI, Jiading district and Xinwei Group
- **Sep 2017** — 8-inch R&D pilot line online — China's first 'More than Moore' pilot fab
- **Jul 2018** — Silicon photonics pilot line (municipal major special project) completes, tape-out capability demonstrated
